status_summary: H.R. 1 (Public Law 119-21, signed 2025-07-04) set new immigration fees, and a USCIS interim final rule published 2026-04-29 (effective 2026-05-29) codifies a minimum 100 dollar asylum application fee, a 100 dollar annual fee while an asylum application is pending, and a rule that these fees cannot be waived or reduced; FY2027 inflation amounts published 2026-10-01 raised the annual asylum fee to 105 dollars from 2026-10-16. A court in Maryland stayed the annual asylum fee guidance on 2025-10-30 and lifted the stay on 2026-02-02, and that case is ongoing. A rule published 2026-01-12 raised premium processing fees by 5.72 percent for inflation without adding forms, a proposal of 2026-06-23 would raise the naturalization fee and end its waivers and reduced fee, a proposal of 2026-08-25 would add an H-1B petition fee, and a final EB-5 fee rule of 2026-09-30 takes effect 2026-11-30. A comprehensive rule raising all USCIS fees was not found.

timeline.event: H.R. 1 (Public Law 119-21) was signed, setting new immigration fees including an asylum application fee and an annual fee while an asylum application is pending, with no waivers or reductions and yearly inflation adjustment.
timeline.source: Federal Register (USCIS interim final rule describing the law)

timeline.event: DHS announced it would begin collecting the 1,000 dollar parole fee required by H.R. 1.
The District of Maryland temporarily stayed USCIS and EOIR guidance on collecting the annual asylum fee in Asylum Seeker Advocacy Project v. USCIS.
DHS published FY2026 inflation adjustments for certain H.R. 1 fees (parole, ESTA, EVUS).
DHS published a rule raising premium processing fees for inflation, effective 2026-03-01; it did not add forms or classifications.
The court lifted its stay and denied a new temporary restraining order and injunction request on the annual asylum fee.
USCIS published an interim final rule (effective 2026-05-29) codifying H.R. 1 fees, including the asylum application fee, the annual asylum fee and no waivers or reductions for them.

USCIS proposed raising the naturalization application fee (Form N-400 from 760 to 1,330 dollars on paper) and ending the reduced fee and fee waivers for Forms N-400 and N-336, keeping the statutory exemption for military members; comments closed 2026-08-24.

USCIS proposed a new 103,265 dollar fee on H-1B cap-subject petitions, payable at filing in addition to other fees and based on its cost-recovery fee authority; comments closed 2026-09-24 and a correction followed on 2026-09-10.

USCIS published a final EB-5 fee rule based on a revised fee study, effective 2026-11-30, raising the Integrity Fund fees for inflation (Form I-526E from 1,000 to 1,100 dollars; regional center fees from 10,000 to 11,000 dollars, or 20,000 to 22,000 dollars for certain centers) and adding a 75 dollar technology fee for Forms I-526 and I-526E; it makes no premium processing changes.
USCIS published FY2027 inflation adjustments to H.R. 1 immigration fees, effective 2026-10-16, raising the annual asylum fee to 105 dollars and leaving the initial asylum fee at 100 dollars.

title: Raise USCIS fees, limit waivers, add an asylum fee, expand premium processing
uncertainties: The interim final rule was read in large part, but the amounts of some H.R. 1 fees (parole, special immigrant juvenile, TPS work permits) were taken from the FY2027 notice rather than the rule. The Clearinghouse page shows no docket entries after 2026-02-20, so later rulings, including on a motion to dismiss filed 2026-02-17, are unknown. A 2024 USCIS fee rule predates the period and was not reviewed. The final EB-5 rule's fee table is an image, so its form fee amounts for Forms I-526, I-526E, I-829 and I-956 were not confirmed; the rule is final but not yet effective. The H-1B fee proposal would recover costs of several agencies, not only USCIS, and was read only in part. An Immigration and Customs Enforcement proposal of 2026-10-08 for Optional Practical Training fees charged to schools and a CBP rule of 2026-08-10 on a statutory biometric fee are not USCIS fee rules and were not counted. No final rule on the naturalization proposal and no new premium processing rule after 2026-01-12 were found in the Federal Register through 2026-10-23. The Mandate's request for fees tied to cost is only partly matched because the fees found are statutory minimums, inflation adjustments, one category-specific final rule and proposals. Progress stays at 45 because the general fee increase and the waiver limits beyond H.R. 1 fees are only proposed and premium processing was not expanded.
